title: A/B Test Strategies That Work
intro: An A/B test only compares the variations you put into it. Clean mechanics can't rescue a weak variation.

learn.title: One win, four explanations
learn.text:
A bigger, brighter, more urgent button gets more clicks. That single result is consistent with four different problems:

• It was easier to find
• The copy was clearer
• It pulled attention away from other information
• Urgency pushed people into a premature action

Each needs a different fix — and the test can't tell you which.

try.q: A more prominent button wins on clicks. What do you know?
options: That the button is easier to find
That the page is more usable overall
try.explain: Four explanations fit the same result.

learn.title: Ground the variation
learn.text:
**Weak:** “we think this version will perform better.”

**Strong:** “users miss the primary action because the label is vague and disconnected from the task; a specific label will increase completion.”

The hypothesis has to name **the cause**, not just predict the outcome. That's what makes the result interpretable afterwards.

try.q: What is missing from “we think this version will perform better”?
try.explain: Without a cause, a win teaches you nothing.

learn.title: Match the claim to the change, and add guardrails
learn.text:
Change **one thing** if you want a narrow claim. Change a **bundle** and you may only compare packages, not elements.

Add **guardrail metrics** so a win on clicks doesn't hide a loss elsewhere — refunds, support contacts, downstream completion.

And when the meeting stalls and someone says “let's just A/B test it”, don't refuse. Slow the team down enough to ask what the variation is actually testing.

try.q: You redesign the whole page and version B wins. What can you claim?
options: The new layout caused the lift
try.explain: A bundled change supports only a bundled claim.

test.q: What does an A/B test compare?
options: Your design against the market standard
test.explain: Which is why the variation matters more than the mechanics.

test.q: What is a guardrail metric for?
options: Catching harm the primary metric hides
test.explain: A click win can hide a refund loss.

test.q: What should you do when someone says “let's just A/B test it”?
options: Ask what the variation is testing
Run it with a smaller sample first
Convert it to a multivariate test
test.explain: Slow the team down without blocking them.

test.q: Why does “winning isn't the same as learning”?
options: A win doesn't tell you which cause produced it
Teams stop testing after a win
test.explain: That's the point of the four-explanations example.

test.q: When can you make a narrow causal claim?
options: When the test ran for two weeks
test.explain: Match the claim to what actually changed.
